headline: Why Your Interior Paint Job Might Not Last: Common Mistakes to Avoid
articleBody:
Ever wonder why a new interior paint job sometimes starts looking rough way too soon? It's frustrating when your beautiful new walls don't hold up like you expected. Often, it comes down to a few common blunders that, once you know them, are totally avoidable. Getting a long-lasting, professional finish isn't just about the paint itself; it's about the process. Here are some frequent mistakes and how you can steer clear of them for your next project.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. Painting over dirty or greasy walls: If your walls aren't clean, the paint won't adhere properly. Always wash your walls thoroughly, especially in kitchens or high-traffic areas, to remove any grime. 
2. Skipping necessary repairs: Don't just paint over holes, cracks, or loose paint. These imperfections will show right through your new coat. Take the time to spackle, sand, and smooth everything out beforehand.
3. Not priming when needed: While not every wall needs primer, it's crucial for bare drywall, patched areas, or when making a drastic color change. Primer helps paint stick better and ensures an even color.
4. Recoating too soon: It's tempting to rush, but applying a second coat before the first is properly dry can lead to peeling, cracking, or an uneven finish. Always check the paint can's instructions for recommended drying and recoat times; humidity generally extends drying time.
5. Failing to protect your surroundings: Paint gets everywhere! Neglecting to cover floors, furniture, and hardware means you'll spend more time cleaning up messes than enjoying your new walls. Proper masking and drop cloths are your best friends.
6. Ignoring ventilation: Poor ventilation means paint odors linger and drying times increase. Open windows and use fans to help air circulate, improving both the drying process and your comfort.
7. Painting over mildew: Mildew needs to be treated and removed, not just painted over. It will grow back through the new paint, ruining your finish and potentially impacting indoor air quality.
